sheet-1-1.description: The lower half of sheet 1 shows the western edge of the Wyoming district on the line between Millburn and South Orange townships, drawn at 100 ft to an inch with Prospect Avenue across the top and Wyoming Avenue across the bottom. Between them lie four long blocks divided by Cypress, Pine, Elm and Maple, with Mountain Avenue along the right edge; Pine, Elm and Maple are marked as not graded. The blocks are laid out in narrow building lots, most of them still vacant in 1912. Frame dwellings with stables and outbuildings stand mainly in the block between Cypress and Pine and along Prospect Avenue and Mountain Avenue, with a few houses in the Elm and Maple blocks. North of Prospect Avenue the ground is cut into large, deep tracts running up to the South Mountain Reservation, which is lettered along the top of this half; a single dwelling stands in the tract at the right. Street widths are marked: 60 ft for Prospect Avenue, 75 ft for Wyoming Avenue and 50 to 60 ft for the cross streets. The row of blocks south of Wyoming Avenue is cut off at the bottom edge and continues on sheet 3; sheet 68 of the Millburn series adjoins on the left. The upper half of the sheet is a separate strip continuing the same street eastward from Mountain Avenue.
notes: Prospect Avenue here is today Sagamore Road; Cypress, Pine, Elm and Maple are Cypress Street, Pine Street, Elm Street and Maple Street (OpenStreetMap).

Millburn and South Orange Townships, Wyoming district on the township line. 100 ft. Two parts split by a heavy line: 1 lower half (Prospect Av = Sagamore Road, Wyoming Av, Cypress, Pine, Elm, Maple, Mountain Av; 10 points); 2 upper half continuing east along Wyoming Av from Mountain Av to Hickory Drive (Clinton, Ridgewood Terrace, Curtiss Pl, Fairview Ter, Sagamore Rd), control mostly along Wyoming Av plus a hand-picked Fairview/Sagamore point.

sheet-1-2.description: The upper half of sheet 1 is a separate strip of the same district, continuing eastward along Wyoming Avenue from Mountain Avenue, drawn at 100 ft to an inch. It shows the line between Millburn Township and South Orange Township, a dash-dot boundary that crosses the strip diagonally and is lettered with both township names. Wyoming Avenue runs along the bottom, with Mountain Avenue at the left, Clinton Avenue (not graded), and the ends of Ridgewood Terrace, Curtiss Place and Hickory Drive meeting it from below. A short stretch of Prospect Avenue appears at the upper left beside Mountain Avenue. To the right, Fairview Terrace and Sagamore Road start together at a tract line and run off the right edge, Sagamore Road at an angle towards sheet 2. The ground is almost entirely undeveloped: large tracts and a row of deep lots along the top border the South Mountain Reservation, lettered across the top edge. Buildings are few: one dwelling and outbuilding between Mountain Avenue and Clinton Avenue, two dwellings between Fairview Terrace and Sagamore Road, and a small building at the right edge. Street widths of 50, 60 and 75 ft are marked. The blocks south of Wyoming Avenue, numbered 3 and 5, are cut off at the heavy dividing line and continue on sheets 3 and 5.
notes: Prospect Avenue here is today Sagamore Road; Curtiss Place is Curtis Place (OpenStreetMap).
Fairview Terrace / Sagamore Road is a hand-picked point at the drawn west end of both streets; the other control lies along Wyoming Avenue, so the fit rests mostly on one line.

Millburn and South Orange Townships, Wyoming district on the township line. 100 ft. Two parts split by a heavy line: 1 lower half (Prospect Av = Sagamore Road, Wyoming Av, Cypress, Pine, Elm, Maple, Mountain Av; 10 points); 2 upper half continuing east along Wyoming Av from Mountain Av to Hickory Drive (Clinton, Ridgewood Terrace, Curtiss Pl, Fairview Ter, Sagamore Rd), control mostly along Wyoming Av plus a hand-picked Fairview/Sagamore point.

sheet-2-1.description: The right strip of sheet 2 shows the ground on the west side of Wyoming Avenue between the South Mountain Reservation and Wyoming Avenue, from Cedar Lane southward, drawn at 100 ft to an inch with Wyoming Avenue running down the right edge. Cedar Lane crosses the top of the strip and meets Wyoming Avenue at the upper right corner; at the upper left a short stretch of South Orange Avenue meets Cedar Lane at an angle. A heavy line divides this strip from the left strip of the sheet, and the South Mountain Reservation is lettered along it. Almost the whole strip is the estate of Mrs. J. B. Osborne, with her dwelling, a stable and several outbuildings in the upper part of the grounds; the rest is open land divided into a few large tracts by straight property lines. No other street is drawn. A narrow way opens off the far side of Wyoming Avenue in the lower half, and block references to sheets 7 and 6 stand across Wyoming Avenue on the right, sheet 8 at the top and block 2 at the bottom. Street widths of 50 ft for Cedar Lane and 75 ft for Wyoming Avenue are marked.
notes: Cedar Lane is today Cedar Lane West (OpenStreetMap).
South Orange Avenue is drawn close to Cedar Lane at the upper left; the modern South Orange Avenue runs about 280 m further north, so the old road has been realigned.
Placed from one hand-picked point, Cedar Lane West / Wyoming Avenue, with the atlas scale and the rotation of the left strip of this sheet (derived second point); low confidence.

West side of Wyoming Av along the South Mountain Reservation. 100 ft, turned (rotation about -37). Two strips split by a heavy line: 1 right strip, Mrs. J. B. Osborne estate south of Cedar Lane (= Cedar Lane West), anchored on a hand-picked Cedar Lane West / Wyoming point; 2 left strip, Claremont Av, Durand Rd, Sagamore Rd, Fairview Ter (two detected points plus hand-picked Fairview/Sagamore). Modern Sagamore/Wyoming junction about 15 m off the drawn one, not used.

sheet-2-2.description: The left strip of sheet 2 shows the west side of Wyoming Avenue in South Orange Township between the South Mountain Reservation and Wyoming Avenue, drawn at 100 ft to an inch with Wyoming Avenue running down the right side next to the heavy dividing line. Claremont Avenue runs diagonally from the reservation at the left to Wyoming Avenue near the top, and Durand Road, marked as not graded, crosses below it, so that the two enclose a large wedge of land with a dwelling, a stable and outbuildings. Further down, Sagamore Road runs diagonally from Wyoming Avenue to the bottom of the strip, and Fairview Terrace runs parallel to the left edge to meet it there. The block between them and the reservation is laid out in narrow building lots, with a few dwellings, one of them plastered, and a small building on Sagamore Road. The top of the strip holds two more dwellings near Wyoming Avenue. A dash-dot line lettered South Orange Township and Millburn Township crosses the lower left corner. The South Mountain Reservation is lettered along the left edge. Block references 6 and 5 stand in Wyoming Avenue for the sheets across the avenue, and block 1 at the bottom continues on sheet 1.
notes: The modern Sagamore Road / Wyoming Avenue junction lies about 15 m from the drawn one and was not used.

Fairview Terrace / Sagamore Road is a hand-picked point at the drawn meeting point of both streets; with Claremont Avenue / Wyoming Avenue and Durand Road / Wyoming Avenue it is one of three points, an exact fit; low to medium confidence.

West side of Wyoming Av along the South Mountain Reservation. 100 ft, turned (rotation about -37). Two strips split by a heavy line: 1 right strip, Mrs. J. B. Osborne estate south of Cedar Lane (= Cedar Lane West), anchored on a hand-picked Cedar Lane West / Wyoming point; 2 left strip, Claremont Av, Durand Rd, Sagamore Rd, Fairview Ter (two detected points plus hand-picked Fairview/Sagamore). Modern Sagamore/Wyoming junction about 15 m off the drawn one, not used.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the southern part of the Wyoming district, on the line between South Orange Township and Millburn Township, which crosses the sheet diagonally from upper left to lower right. The drawing is turned so that Wyoming Avenue runs down the left edge and Ridgewood Road, beside the Morris and Essex Division of the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad, runs down the right. Ridgewood Terrace borders the top, with a row of numbered frame dwellings on narrow lots between it and Clinton Avenue. South of Clinton Avenue is a deeper tract with scattered dwellings and St. George's Episcopal Church with its rectory. Mountain Avenue crosses the sheet below it. Farther down, the blocks between Wyoming Avenue and Myrtle Avenue are cut by Maple, Elm, Pine and Cypress into long narrow building lots, mostly vacant, with a few dwellings and, at the bottom, the Wyoming Public School, a fireproof building of reinforced concrete. East of Myrtle Avenue a large undivided tract holds scattered houses, and in its lower part C. R. Bailey's works for the manufacture of talcum powder, heated by steam and lit and powered by electricity. The railroad, four tracks, passes in the lower right with the Jerome Avenue and Rosedale Avenue street ends beyond it. Street widths are marked at 50 and 60 feet, and 75 feet for Wyoming Avenue. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Sheet 1 adjoins on the left above, sheet 68 of the Millburn series on the left below, sheet 4 on the right and sheet 69 at the bottom right.
notes: The label at the right edge of the Mountain Avenue block reads 'Mountrin Av.' as printed (the left-hand label reads 'Mountain Av.'); Mountain Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Maple, Elm, Pine and Cypress are printed without a suffix; they are today Maple Street, Elm Street, Pine Street and Cypress Street (OpenStreetMap).
Drawn Ridgewood Road junctions (with Mountain Avenue and Clinton Avenue) sit 3 to 4 m off their modern positions; those junctions were left out of the fit.
Myrtle Avenue south of Maple Street and the Cypress Street end at the bottom edge are off their modern lines by 7 to 10 m and were not used.

Wyoming / Ridgewood district on the Millburn line, turned (rot -36.6): Wyoming Av, Myrtle Av, Maple, Elm, Pine, Mountain Av. 100 ft. Ridgewood Rd, Myrtle at Elm and Pine and Cypress junctions left out (3.5-10 m off).

sheet-4-1.description: The lower part of sheet 4 lies south of a heavy dividing line that crosses the sheet from upper left to lower right, and is drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Its main feature is the four-track railroad of the Morristown and Essex Division of the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western, which runs diagonally from the upper left to the lower right and is crossed by Ridgewood Road on a bridge. Ridgewood Road is drawn twice, once along the upper left of the part and once as a nearly level street on the right of the bridge. In the lower left, the parallel streets Oakdale, Roland and Rosedale Avenues run down from Ridgewood Road to Milton, cutting the land into very long, narrow building lots numbered in blocks 7, 8 and 9. Almost all of these lots are vacant, with a few frame dwellings scattered along them. The line between Millburn Township and South Orange Township crosses the part as a dash-dot line running from the lower left towards the bridge. Just east of it stands the Public Service Gas Company's emergency station, with a gas tank, beside the railroad. In the lower right Pierson Road and two unnamed streets enclose a mostly empty block with two dwellings. Ridgewood Road on the right is lined by a few dwellings and a barn. A large area in the middle, between the railroad and the blocks, is blank. Street widths are marked at 50 and 60 feet. Sheets 48 and 49 adjoin on the right and at the bottom, and sheet 69 of the Millburn series on the left.
notes: Roland Avenue is Cypress Street in OpenStreetMap, between Oakdale Avenue and Rosedale Avenue; Milton is Milton Street.
Cypress Street / Ridgewood Road was detected about 8 m off its modern position and rejected.
Control points lie only in the left half; the right-hand blocks rest on the fitted scale and rotation (modern Pierson Road projects onto the drawn one).

100 ft. Two parts split by a heavy line: 1 lower (Oakdale, Roland Av = Cypress Street, Rosedale, Milton, railroad); 2 upper (Ridgewood Rd, Mountrin = Mountain Av, Clinton, Winthrop, Lenox, Railroad Av = Maplewood Avenue). Drawn railroad about 20 m from the modern line.

sheet-4-2.description: The upper part of sheet 4 lies north of the heavy dividing line and shows the area on both sides of Ridgewood Road where it meets Mountrin, Clinton, Winthrop and Lenox streets, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Ridgewood Road runs along the top of the part, with Mountrin Avenue, Clinton Avenue, Ridgewood Terrace and Curtiss Place entering it from the north and Mountrin Avenue, Winthrop Place, Lenox Place and Baker running south from it. The blocks between are laid out in regular narrow lots, with a good number of frame dwellings, particularly along Winthrop Place and Lenox Place. Maplewood M. E. Church, a large building coloured as a brick structure, stands at the head of Lenox Place with its Sunday school beside it. South of the houses the four-track railroad of the Morris and Essex Division of the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western runs diagonally from the upper left to the lower right, with Jerome Avenue along its upper side and Railroad Avenue between the railroad and the ends of the residential streets. At the left, Pierson Road and a street marked Not Named enclose vacant ground, and South Mountrin Avenue runs down towards the dividing line. The lower right corner shows Maplewood Avenue and a portion of Jerome Avenue. A compass rose stands near the dividing line. Street widths are marked at 50 feet. Sheets 3 and 5 adjoin above, 48 on the right, and 49 below on the left.
notes: 'Mountrin' is the printed spelling on this sheet (and on the right side of sheet 3); Mountain Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Curtiss Place is Curtis Place, Baker is Baker Street and Everett Place is Everitt Place today (OpenStreetMap).
Railroad Avenue is the street along the railroad, now Maplewood Avenue; junctions with it that sit against the tracks (Lenox Place, Baker) were left out.
The drawn railroad lies about 20 m from its modern line (rail check).

100 ft. Two parts split by a heavy line: 1 lower (Oakdale, Roland Av = Cypress Street, Rosedale, Milton, railroad); 2 upper (Ridgewood Rd, Mountrin = Mountain Av, Clinton, Winthrop, Lenox, Railroad Av = Maplewood Avenue). Drawn railroad about 20 m from the modern line.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 shows the part of the Wyoming district between Wyoming Avenue along the top and Ridgewood Road along the bottom, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that the streets run at an angle to the sheet edges. Four long north-south streets, Ridgewood Terrace, Curtiss Place, Hickory Drive and Kermit Road, run down the sheet, crossed in the upper middle by Roosevelt Road, and Durand Road forms the right edge. The blocks are laid out in uniform narrow lots with a regular row of frame dwellings, each with its number, along Ridgewood Terrace and Curtiss Place and a looser scatter in the other blocks. The block between Curtiss Place and Hickory Drive and the northern block between Wyoming Avenue and Roosevelt Road are mostly vacant. At the junction of Kermit Road and Roosevelt Road stands a large building of terra cotta brick, coloured as a masonry structure, with a smaller one beside it. Quentin Court runs across to Durand Road in the lower right, enclosing a block with a few houses. Ridgewood Road crosses the bottom of the sheet, with Lenox Place, Baker, Highland Place and Everett Place running south from it on the lower part, and a large open tract with scattered dwellings to the right. Sagamore Road enters at the top and a compass rose stands at the right edge. Street widths are marked at 30 to 60 feet. Sheets 1 and 2 adjoin above, 3 and 4 on the left, 6 on the right, and 47 and 48 below.
notes: The street printed Roosevelt Road across the upper middle is Kermit Road today, and the one printed Kermit Road is today's Roosevelt Road (OpenStreetMap).
Curtiss Place is Curtis Place, Baker is Baker Street and Everett Place is Everitt Place today.
Junctions with Curtis Place / Kermit Road, Durand Road / Wyoming Avenue and Baker Street / Everitt Place were left out (5 to 7 m off the drawn position).
Curtis Place / Ridgewood Road was not detected.
100 ft. Wyoming Av to Ridgewood Rd: Ridgewood Terrace, Curtiss Pl, Hickory Dr, Roosevelt and Kermit roads, Durand Rd, Baker / Everett Pl.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 lies east of sheet 5 and covers the Wyoming district blocks between Wyoming Avenue along the top and Ridgewood Road, which crosses the lower third from lower left to right, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Durand Road forms the left edge, with Quentin Court entering it. Euclid Avenue and Claremont Avenue run down between Wyoming Avenue and Ridgewood Road, and a street marked only Drive forms the right edge. The Euclid Avenue and Claremont Avenue blocks have a loose scatter of frame dwellings, with a row of lots along Euclid Avenue. East of Claremont Avenue the large tract is cut by Sycamore Avenue and Hemlock Avenue, and holds the buildings of Colinwood Farm (Dairy), with barns, stables and silos along the right side, a reinforced concrete building and a house in the lower part. South of Ridgewood Road, Durand Road curves away at the left and Jefferson Avenue runs down to Kendall Avenue at the bottom. At the lower right, Carthwaite Terrace and Hoffman are laid out with rows of narrow lots, with Headley Place entering at the edge and Beech Place a short street at the bottom. A large open tract lies between Durand Road and Jefferson Avenue. A compass rose stands in the lower left. Street widths are marked at 25 to 75 feet. Sheets 2 and 7 adjoin above and on the right, 5 on the left, and 46 and 47 below.
notes: 'Colinwood' is the printed spelling; the street is Collinwood Road today, and the unnamed 'Drive' on the right is probably its predecessor.
Carthwaite Terrace is Garthwaite Terrace, Hoffman is Hoffman Street and Kendall Avenue is Kendal Avenue today (OpenStreetMap).
Claremont Avenue / Ridgewood Road, Jefferson Avenue / Ridgewood Road and Hoffman Street / Kendal Avenue were 4 to 6 m off the drawn position and left out.
The fitted scale is about 2 percent above that of neighbouring sheets.
100 ft. Euclid, Claremont, Colinwood Farm, Ridgewood Rd, Jefferson Av. Fitted scale 2.3 percent above neighbours; Ridgewood Rd junctions left out.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 lies east of sheet 6 and shows the eastern end of the Wyoming district, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Wyoming Avenue, a 75 foot street, runs across the top and Kendall Avenue across the bottom. Ridgewood Road crosses the lower third, bending at its left third, with a street marked only Drive and Hoffman forming the left edge. Most of the sheet is open land: the large undivided tract between Wyoming Avenue and Ridgewood Road holds only a few small buildings and, near the centre, a compass rose, while the lower left has a block of narrow lots on Hoffman, with Headley Place running across below it. Along Ridgewood Road, in the middle and right, stand scattered frame dwellings and, at the right, a carpenter and machine shop; south of the road a small cluster of dwellings and a larger long building cluster around the middle block. At the right, Cedar Lane runs up the sheet from Ridgewood Road, with Lenox Terrace and Lenox Place meeting it, and East Cedar Lane runs down beside it to Kendall Avenue between two blocks of narrow lots and a few dwellings. Audley forms the right edge below Ridgewood Road. The boundary line between South Orange Township and South Orange Village runs up the right side as a dash-dot line, and is lettered along it. Street widths are marked at 25 to 75 feet. Sheets 2 and 6 adjoin on the left and above, 46 below and 9 on the right.
notes: Hoffman is Hoffman Street, Kendall Avenue is Kendal Avenue, Cedar Lane is Cedar Lane West and Audley is Audley Street today (OpenStreetMap).
Cedar Lane West / Lenox Place and / Wyoming Avenue were not detected; Cedar Lane West / Lenox Terrace is used.
The 'Drive' along the upper left edge continues Hoffman north of Ridgewood Road (Collinwood Road today).
100 ft. Hoffman, Ridgewood Rd, Cedar Lane, Kendall Av; township / village line.

sheet-31.description: Sheet 31 shows the northeastern edge of South Orange Township along Irvington Avenue, at the Newark city line, drawn at 100 ft to an inch with the street grid turned so that Irvington Avenue runs from the upper left corner diagonally to the lower right. Ward Place runs up the left edge of the sheet from Irvington Avenue. The only built-up part is a narrow strip of long, deep lots along Ward Place at the upper left, where a row of frame dwellings and a few outbuildings stand, and a group of frame buildings and sheds behind them on the Emma A. Harrison property. The rest of the area north of Irvington Avenue is large unbuilt tracts with owners' names (Mary A. Hughes, Ludwig Batt, Emma A. Harrison, William Heyeek). A dash-dot line crossing the sheet from the lower left to the upper right is the boundary between South Orange Village and South Orange Township. The wide blank area at the right is lettered City of Newark and is not drawn. South of Irvington Avenue only the ends of Turrel Street, Lindsley, Wetmore, Essex, Union and Hudson avenues are shown, each cut off at the edge of the sheet; they are drawn in full on sheets 42 and 43. Water pipes are marked along Ward Place and Irvington Avenue. Boyden Avenue appears at the lower right corner where it meets Irvington Avenue, continuing on sheet 32. Neighbouring sheets are 27 at the left, 29 at the top, 32 at the right, 42 at the lower left and 43 at the bottom.
notes: Turrel Street is today Waverly Place (OpenStreetMap), matched by position and spacing from Lindsley Avenue; sheet 42 letters the same street Turrell.
Irvington Avenue is drawn about 50 ft wide, narrower than the 75 ft right-of-way in the modern parcels.

sheet-32.description: Sheet 32 shows an almost undeveloped corner of South Orange Township north of Irvington Avenue, on the border of the City of Newark, drawn at 100 ft to an inch. Irvington Avenue runs along the bottom edge from the corner of Boyden Avenue at the lower left to a bend where it turns off the sheet towards sheet 44. Above it the sheet is divided into large farm and estate tracts with the owners' names: J. B. Bradbury, Wm Elsman, J. E. Brown, Amos F. Brown, J. Kranke, Jas. Bradbury, A. G. & C. N. Brown and M. N. Vail, with two tracts lettered City of Newark. A dash-dot boundary line runs from top to bottom right of the centre, and the area to its right is lettered City of Newark. Buildings stand only along Irvington Avenue: on the J. B. Bradbury tract a group of four long greenhouses with a dwelling, stable and coop, and further along a few dwellings, a wagon shed, a coop and a plastered building near the bend. Lot letters A to L mark the frontages along Irvington Avenue. No other street is drawn, which is why the sheet was placed from two corners of Irvington Avenue carried from sheet 44. Sheet 31 adjoins on the left, sheet 30 at the top and sheet 44 at the bottom.
notes: The ground of this sheet lies today within the City of Newark; the boundary drawn here is not today's.
Elsman Terrace, a modern street in this area, carries the name of the Wm Elsman tract.
Placed from two corners of Irvington Avenue carried from sheet 44 (helmert); low confidence.

Open tracts north of Irvington Av on the City of Newark line (today in Newark). 100 ft. No street but Irvington Av; placed from two corners of Irvington Av carried from sheet 44 (helmert); low confidence.

sheet-41.description: Sheet 41 covers the north-eastern part of South Orange Village and Township around Prospect Street, Summit Avenue and Richmond Avenue, drawn at 100 ft to an inch with the page turned so that Prospect Street runs across the top and then curves up to the right. At the upper left is a regular grid of two long blocks, numbered 1 and 2, between Prospect, Summit and Richmond avenues, Vassar Place and Garfield Place, with frame dwellings on narrow lots, a brick building (coloured pink) at the end of the upper block, and water pipes marked in the streets. A dash-dot line crossing the sheet diagonally is the boundary between South Orange Village and South Orange Township. Baldwin Road leaves the lower left corner. East of Garfield Place lie scattered dwellings and a farm group on large lots along Prospect Street; at the upper right Montague Place and Tichenor Avenue bound blocks of narrow lots, and Fifth Street meets Prospect Street at the top. In the east and south a block of narrow lots is laid out between Miller, Fairview Avenue, West Ward Place, Grand Avenue and Van Bushkirk, along South 4th Street, still with no buildings. Garfield Place, Essex Avenue and South appear at the foot of the sheet. Large parts of the sheet are blank, belonging to sheets 55 and 56 at the left and 42 at the right. Neighbouring sheets are 40 at the top, 39 at the upper left, 38 and 36 at the right, 42 at the lower right, 43 at the bottom, 56 at the lower left and 55 at the left.
notes: Prospect is today Prospect Street, Roland Avenue and Prospect Place keep their names (OpenStreetMap).

The street lettered Vassar Place is today Baldwin Road north of Richmond Avenue (OpenStreetMap), matched by position: the detected Baldwin Road junctions with Summit and Richmond avenues fall on the drawn Vassar Place.
Grand Avenue and Van Bushkirk have no counterpart in OpenStreetMap; sheet 42 prints the second as Van Buskirk.
The upper-left block grid is well controlled; the lower and right parts of the sheet have no control points.
Garfield Place / Prospect Street and Garfield Place / Tichenor Avenue were rejected by the detector (about 9.5 m from the fit).
100 ft. Prospect / Summit / Richmond / Vassar Pl (= Baldwin Road) grid of South Orange Village; upper left controlled, rest mostly blank. Garfield Pl junctions rejected (9-10 m).

sheet-42.description: Sheet 42 covers a hillside block of the Village and Township of South Orange south of Irvington Avenue,. It is the only sheet of this group drawn at 50 ft to an inch (scale of feet 0 to 150). Irvington Avenue crosses the top of the sheet from left to right; Turrell, Lindsley and Wetmore avenues run south from it to a street lettered South, which crosses the sheet near the bottom. Between them are two long, narrow blocks cut into deep, narrow lots with frame dwellings, most with house numbers along the street fronts, and a third block at the right. West Ward Place runs down the left side of the sheet in a long wedge, with a junk yard and wagon shed at its lower end. Below South Street the lots are mostly vacant and the sheet is crossed by Grand Avenue and Van Buskirk Avenue running south to S. 4th Street, which crosses the bottom edge. A dash-dot line running from the lower left towards the top is the boundary between South Orange Village and South Orange Township. Water pipes are marked in Irvington Avenue, Turrell Avenue and Lindsley Avenue. Neighbouring sheets are 31 at the top, 36 at the left, 43 at the right and 41 at the bottom.
notes: The street lettered Turrell is today Waverly Place (OpenStreetMap), matched by position and spacing from Lindsley Avenue; sheet 31 letters the same street Turrel Street.
The street lettered South is today South 4th Street (OpenStreetMap), whose junctions with Lindsley and Wetmore avenues fit the drawing to under 1 m.
The street lettered S. 4th St. along the bottom edge, and Grand Avenue and Van Buskirk, have no counterpart in OpenStreetMap and were not used.
The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch; the other sheets of the atlas covered here are at 100 ft.
50 ft to an inch. Irvington Avenue to South 4th Street: Turrell (= Waverly Place), Lindsley, Wetmore, W. Ward Pl.

sheet-43.description: Sheet 43 covers a corner of South Orange Township between Irvington Avenue at the top and Parker Avenue at the bottom, drawn at 100 ft to an inch with the street grid turned so that Irvington Avenue curves across the upper right of the page. Only the upper left is laid out in blocks: Essex, Union and Hudson avenues run down the page from Irvington Avenue to Garfield Place, crossed in the middle by a street lettered South and, at the left edge, by S. 4th Street. The blocks between them are numbered 1 to 6 and cut into deep, narrow lots that were still almost entirely vacant in 1912; the only buildings are a few frame dwellings on Union Avenue and two on the block at the top, between Union and Hudson. Garfield Place closes the laid-out area at the bottom, and below it the streets stop at a blank edge. The rest of the sheet is open ground with no streets drawn, except Boyden Avenue, which runs down the right side from Irvington Avenue to a triangular island where it meets Parker Avenue, and Parker Avenue itself, which crosses the lower part of the page from the lower left to the right. A farm group of frame buildings, a small blue-coloured building and sheds stands near the junction of Boyden and Parker avenues. Highland Avenue is lettered at the bottom edge where it meets Parker Avenue. Neighbouring sheets are 42 at the upper left, 41 at the left, 56 at the lower left, 62 at the bottom, 44 at the right and 31 at the top.
notes: The street lettered South is today South 4th Street (OpenStreetMap); the junctions with Essex, Union and Hudson avenues fit to within 3 m.
Irvington Avenue is drawn about 50 ft wide, narrower than the 75 ft right-of-way in the modern parcels.
Boyden Avenue and Parker Avenue form a triangle at the lower right, as on sheet 44; the junction was not used for control.
The modern Boyden Avenue / Garfield Place junction is not drawn and was not used.
100 ft. Essex, Union, Hudson to Garfield Place; Irvington and Parker avenues.

sheet-44.description: Sheet 44 covers the south-eastern corner of South Orange Township (today Maplewood) where it met the City of Newark and the Town of Irvington, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned on the page: Irvington Avenue runs down the right edge from Boyden Avenue, bends at the lower right and runs diagonally down to the lower left, where it meets Florence Avenue and Clinton Avenue West. Boyden Avenue crosses the top from the left edge, past a small triangular junction with Parker Avenue, to Irvington Avenue at the upper right. Most of the sheet is open land in a few large tracts: a big tract fills the centre, with the C. J. Wilson and Elizabeth E. Hogan properties and their dwellings, stables and outbuildings in its lower half. A small row of houses stands on Boyden Avenue at the upper left. Along Irvington Avenue near the bend there is a cluster of dwellings, shops and stables, and the fire house of Ivy Hill Hose Co. No. 4. The lower left corner shows built-up lots of the neighbouring town along Laurel Avenue, Franklin, Stephen and Florence Avenue; a dash-dot boundary line crosses it, lettered Newark Volume Five and Town of Irvington, and a second boundary runs across the lower right towards the area lettered City of Newark. Franklin Street and Webster Street are named in the left margin. Sheet 32 adjoins on the right, sheets 43 and 62 at the top and sheet 63 on the left.
notes: The Ivy Hill Hose Co. No. 4 fire house stands on Irvington Avenue near its bend.
Parker Avenue north of Boyden Avenue is drawn; the modern Parker Avenue also runs south-east from the same junction across the big tract, which was open land in 1912.
Placed from three points only (Boyden Avenue / Irvington Avenue detected, Boyden Avenue / Parker Avenue and the Irvington Avenue bend at Norman Road / Putnam Street hand-picked); low confidence.

South-east corner of the township: Boyden Av, Parker Av, Irvington Av (bend), Clinton Av W., Florence Av; Irvington and Newark lines. 100 ft, turned (rotation about 75). Three points (one detected, two hand-picked); low confidence.

sheet-46.description: Sheet 46 covers the area between Audley along the top and Jefferson Avenue along the bottom, on the line between South Orange Village and South Orange Township, drawn at 100 feet to an inch although the scale bar printed on it is lettered 0 to 150. A dash-dot line lettered as the village and township boundary crosses the upper part from left to right. At the left, a deep block of very narrow lots runs between Kendall Avenue and Walton Avenue; the lots are drawn but almost all vacant. Weymouth Avenue, Maplewood Avenue and Ormond Avenue run north and south through the middle, where the blocks are large and empty apart from one dwelling and a short street marked Not Named. Maplewood Avenue curves at its upper end to join a diagonal street. The four-track railroad of the Morris and Essex Division of the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western runs down the right of the centre, crossed by Parker Avenue on a bridge, with the East Branch Rahway River winding beside it. At the right, the Sillcocks-Miller Company's celluloid and artificial leather works fills a block between Parker Avenue and Jefferson Avenue, with a row of dwellings on Valley beside it; the works is described as of reinforced concrete and fireproof, with a water supply taken from the brook by a pump. Hixon Place and Arnold Terrace enter at the upper right, and Crowell Avenue and Edgewood Avenue at the lower right. Hoffman Street and Garthwaite Terrace lie at the lower left. Street widths are marked at 50 and 60 feet. Sheets 7 and 6 adjoin above and 47 below, 45 above and 54 to the right.
notes: Audley is Audley Street, Kendall Avenue is Kendal Avenue, Walton Avenue is Walton Road at Jefferson Avenue, Valley is Valley Street, Crowell Avenue is Crowell Place and Edgewood Avenue is Edgewood Place today (OpenStreetMap).
Hixon Place, Weymouth Avenue and Ormond Avenue are not in the modern extract; the Parker Avenue / Valley Street junction was left out (4 m off) and the others are not used.
The printed bar is lettered 0 to 150 feet but the fit gives about 3.97 px per foot, the 100 feet to an inch of the neighbouring sheets.
The drawn railroad lies about 28 m from its modern line; junctions on it were not used.

Scale bar printed 0-150 ft but the sheet fits 100 ft to an inch (3.97 px/ft). Audley, Kendall, Walton, Maplewood Av, Parker Av, Valley St, railroad; Sillcocks-Miller works. Rotation 4.5 degrees from sheet 47 (real).

sheet-47.description: Sheet 47 shows the centre of the Maplewood district, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Jefferson Avenue crosses the top, joined by Walton Avenue, Kendall Avenue and, in the upper right, Dunnell Road. South of it, Woodland Avenue and Maplewood Avenue run down in parallel from Jefferson Avenue to Durand Road, with Beech Place crossing between them at two places; the blocks are laid out in narrow lots with frame dwellings, many numbered, and a church or hall coloured blue near the middle of the Woodland block. The railroad, four tracks of the Morris and Essex Division, runs down the middle of the right half beside Maplewood Avenue, and at the bottom the sheet shows Maplewood Station, the township hall and the fire station of the Maplewood fire company. Durand Road curves in from the left to meet Maplewood Avenue, and Oakland Road, the Y-shaped continuation, runs southwest beside the tracks with N. Burnett and a large open tract to the right. The East Branch Rahway River winds down the right side, with Oakland Road, Valley and Park Place crossing it. George C. Salmon's coal, lumber and masons' supplies yard stands beside Dunnell Road. At the upper right, Lincoln Place, Edgewood Avenue and Crowell Avenue enter from sheet 54. At the lower left, Inwood Place and Highland Place enter with small lots and a stream with its culvert. Street widths are marked at 50 and 60 feet. Sheets 46 above, 6 and 5 to the left, 48 below and 53 and 54 on the right.
notes: Woodland Avenue is Woodland Road, Walton Avenue is Walton Road, Beech Place is Beach Place, Kendall Avenue is Kendal Avenue, Valley is Valley Street and Park Place is Park Road today (OpenStreetMap).
North Burnett: the printed 'N. Burnett' with the prefix written out; no suffix is printed. Burnett Avenue is the modern form of the name.
The Highland Place / Maplewood Avenue, Oakland Road / Valley Street, Durand Road / Woodland Road and Jefferson Avenue / Kendal Avenue junctions were 6 to 9 m from their drawn positions and left out.
The sheet is drawn about 4 degrees differently from sheet 46, which it overlaps along Jefferson Avenue.
The drawn railroad lies about 30 m from its modern line.
100 ft. Maplewood centre: Woodland, Maplewood Av, Durand Rd, Oakland Rd, Jefferson Av, Valley, Maplewood station and railroad. Several junctions 4-9 m off left out.

sheet-48.description: Sheet 48 covers the Maplewood part of South Orange Township, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, with the street grid turned so that the Morris and Essex (Lackawanna) railroad runs diagonally across the top of the page. The railroad is bordered by Jerome Avenue on its south side and Railroad Avenue on its north side. South of the tracks a block of long, narrow lots lies between Salter Place and Burnett, bounded on the left by South Mountain Avenue and on the right by Maple Avenue, with a second row of lots south of Burnett running towards Baker. Houses are scattered along Salter Place, Burnett and Maple Avenue; the Maplewood School stands on Maple Avenue east of the tracks' diagonal, and a few frame dwellings and a store group lie along Baker, North Burnett Street and the Maplewood Avenue end of the sheet. At the top right a compact group of closely built frame houses lines Everett Place and Highland Place, and a stream crosses Maplewood Avenue near the brick municipal buildings. The lower third of the sheet is open ground: the Mill Pond and the East Branch Rahway River, the grounds of the Maplewood Field Club with its club house, and, along Valley at the bottom, a greenhouse range and dairy farm buildings. Park Avenue, Sommer Avenue, Girard Place and Alden Place appear as the ends of streets drawn in full on sheet 52 at the lower left. The sheet is bordered by sheets 4 and 5 above, 49 on the left, 47 on the right, and 52 and 53 below.
notes: Burnett is today Burnet Street, Baker is Baker Street, Valley is Valley Street, Jerome Avenue is Dunnell Road in OpenStreetMap, and Everett Place is Everitt Place.
Several unnamed streets are lettered 'Not Named' on the sheet.
The Maplewood Field Club and the greenhouse are lettered as such on the sheet.
Baker Street / Everitt Place was left out: the modern junction lies 5 m from the drawn one.
100 ft. Salter Pl, Burnett, Maple Av, Baker, Jerome Av (= Dunnell Road), Everett / Highland Pl; railroad across the top.

sheet-49.description: Sheet 49 covers the western edge of South Orange Township where it meets Millburn Township, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned so that Valley runs down the right side of the page. The top third shows a planned residential district of long, narrow, mostly vacant building lots in blocks between South Mountain Avenue, Salter Place, Burnett and Pierson Road, with a few frame dwellings on Salter Place and a street along the left edge lettered 'No Name'. Pierson Road crosses the sheet from left to right and reaches Valley near the top right, where Pierson's Stock Farm, a group of large stable and farm buildings, stands beside the Mill Pond and its feeder stream. Below Pierson Road a second tier of lots and several unnamed roads lead into a large block of open land, crossed from top to bottom by the winding East Branch Rahway River. At the bottom left the dash-dot line between South Orange Township and Millburn Township and the line between Essex County and Union County cross Millburn Avenue at a steel bridge over the river. A small group of frame dwellings and stores, including a hotel, stands along Millburn Avenue, and a few houses line Milton, Rosedale Avenue and Roland Avenue at the lower left, where the sheet adjoins sheet 69. Neighbouring sheets are 48 at the top, 50 on the right and 4 on the left.
notes: Burnett is today Burnet Street, Valley is Valley Street, Milton is Milton Street (OpenStreetMap).
Roland Avenue is Cypress Street in OpenStreetMap, from the position of its junctions with Milton and Millburn Avenue.
Park Avenue is lettered only at the right edge, where the street is drawn in full on sheet 50.
Several streets are lettered 'No Name'.
100 ft. Western edge: South Mountain Av, Salter Pl, Burnett, Pierson Rd, Millburn Av, Rahway River; mostly open land.

sheet-50.description: Sheet 50 covers the border of South Orange Township and Union County on the south side of the Rahway valley, drawn at 100 ft to an inch with the sheet turned so that Valley runs up the left side of the page. Across the top, Park Avenue is lined on its south side by a long row of narrow building lots between Valley and Osborne Terrace, with Alden Place and Hubert Place entering from the north. Below this a large tract of open land is crossed by Pierson Road, which meets Valley at the left, and by a street marked 'Proposed Street'. A few frame houses and farm buildings stand beside Valley. In the lower half Millburn Avenue runs diagonally from the lower left to the right, with the dash-dot line between Essex County and Union County following it. At its lower left end Model Park Company's amusement park stands beside Valley, with a cafe, a dance hall with a platform, a grand stand, a horse shed and a garage with an electrical works. Hollywood Park, a fenced field, occupies the block to its right. At the lower right Springfield Avenue meets Millburn Avenue and Montclair Avenue at the edge of the sheet, with Bryon Avenue, Russell and Vauxhall branching from Springfield Avenue, and a few frame houses on long lots. The neighbouring sheets are 52 above, 49 on the left and 51 on the right.
notes: Valley is today Valley Street, Russell is Russell Street, Bryon Avenue is Byron Terrace (OpenStreetMap).
Vauxhall is lettered on a street at the lower edge; the modern Vauxhall Road lies about 550 m to the west and was not matched to it.
Osborne Terrace is lettered as 'Osborne Ter.' running up the page from Park Avenue.
Several unnamed streets are lettered 'Not Named'.
100 ft. Park Av lots, Pierson Rd, Millburn Av, Essex / Union county line, Model Park; Springfield Av at lower right. Vauxhall not matched.

sheet-51.description: Sheet 51 covers the Springfield Avenue corridor on the border of South Orange Township and Union County, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned so that Springfield Avenue runs diagonally from the lower left to the upper right. Across the top, Park Avenue is lined on its south side by a long row of narrow building lots. Below it the open land holds a dairy farm with several farm buildings beside Springfield Avenue, and a street lettered 'Proposed Street'. East of Springfield Avenue three blocks of long, narrow vacant lots are laid out between Indiana, Ohio, Oregon and Laurel Avenue; they are mostly unbuilt. Laurel Avenue continues south-west as Millburn Avenue, and the dash-dot line between Essex County and Union County follows it. South of this line, a built-up district of frame dwellings and a few outbuildings lies in parallel strips between Montclair Avenue, Hilton Avenue, Oswald Place and Carnegie Place, which run down the page, with the Union Baptist Church between Hilton Avenue and Oswald Place. In the upper right corner a north arrow and parts of Franklin Avenue, Hilton Avenue and Lexington Avenue show the edge of the Hilton district, which is drawn in full on sheet 57. The neighbouring sheets are 52 above, 50 on the left and 57 on the right.
notes: Indiana, Ohio and Oregon are today Indiana Street, Ohio Street and Oregon Street (OpenStreetMap).
Laurel Avenue and Millburn Avenue are one line on the sheet, lettered Laurel Avenue to the east and Millburn Avenue to the west of the junction with Springfield Avenue.
Indiana Street / Laurel Avenue was detected about 12 m from the fit and left out.
100 ft. Springfield Avenue corridor, Indiana / Ohio / Oregon blocks, Laurel and Millburn avenues, county line.

sheet-52.description: Sheet 52 covers the Maplewood district of South Orange Township along Valley and South Prospect, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, with the street grid turned so that Valley curves across the top of the page and South Prospect runs along the bottom. The core of the sheet is a planned residential tract of long, narrow lots set in blocks numbered 1 to 5 between Park Avenue on the left and Girard Place on the right, cut by Hubert Place and Osborne Terrace and divided by Sommer Avenue. Frame dwellings are scattered across these blocks, and a larger building tinted pink stands beside Osborne Terrace. Further right a block of lots reaches from Girard Place across to Tuscan Road, and a row of narrow lots follows the north side of South Prospect, with a pink-tinted building near the right-hand end. South Prospect is the curving street across the lower part of the sheet; Harvard Avenue and Wellesley Avenue enter it from the south. At the lower left a diagonal block of narrow lots lies between Park Avenue and South Prospect, with Bowdoin Street and Cornell Avenue entering South Prospect at the bottom, and Springfield Avenue and a short stretch of South Prospect Street show at the lower left corner where the sheet adjoins sheet 57. The neighbouring sheets are 50 and 51 on the left, 48 above, 53 on the right and 58 below.
notes: South Prospect is today Prospect Street, Valley is Valley Street, Bowdoin Street and Harvard Avenue keep their names (OpenStreetMap).
The south side of South Prospect is drawn as open land belonging to sheet 58.
100 ft. Park Av / Sommer / Girard tract, Valley and South Prospect, Harvard, Bowdoin, Osborne Ter.

sheet-53.description: Sheet 53 covers the Maplewood district of South Orange Township between Valley and South Prospect, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, with the street grid turned so that Valley runs down the left side of the page and South Prospect down the right. The top third is a block of long, narrow lots on the south side of Oakland Road, with frame houses along its frontage and around the Valley end, and the heads of North Terrace and Kensington Terrace entering Oakland Road from the north. A second block below Park Place is a long strip of deep lots fronting Valley, with a few large houses and an outbuilding set back from the road. Private Road, a drive 40 to 50 ft wide, separates this block from a block of narrow lots on Oakview Avenue; the Oakview Avenue frontage holds a row of eight or nine nearly identical frame dwellings and a pink-tinted building farther along the street. The lower half is occupied by the S. P. Brown Estate, a large open tract with a ring drive and two or three houses, and Tuscan Road crosses the bottom of the sheet from Valley to South Prospect. On the right margin the ends of Delaware Avenue, Plymouth Avenue, Madison Avenue, Burnett Terrace and Courter Avenue show where those streets meet South Prospect, drawn in full on sheet 59 and sheet 60. The neighbouring sheets are 54 above, 47 on the left, 48 and 52 below and 59 and 60 on the right.
notes: South Prospect is today Prospect Street, Valley is Valley Street and Park Place is Park Road (OpenStreetMap).
Private Road probably corresponds to the modern Mountain View Terrace.
The ring drive in the S. P. Brown Estate probably corresponds to the modern North Crescent and South Crescent.
The Park Road / Valley Street junction was detected about 12 m from the fit and left out.
100 ft. Oakland Rd to Tuscan Rd along Valley, S. P. Brown estate, Oakview Av, Private Road (= Mountain View Terrace, probable).

sheet-54.description: Sheet 54 covers the area of Maplewood and South Orange between Valley and South Prospect, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, with the street grid turned so that Valley runs up the left side of the page and South Prospect up the right. The title is 'South Orange Village & Township': a dash-dot line crossing the top of the sheet marks the boundary between South Orange Village and South Orange Township, close to Hixon Place and Sherman Place. A few frame houses and farm outbuildings (coops) stand in the upper part, which is mostly open land cut by Academy, Beach and Parker Avenue; Hixon Place and Sherman Place carry closely spaced dwellings along their frontage. Below Parker Avenue the sheet is a regular grid of deep, narrow lots between North Terrace, Kensington Terrace and South Prospect, crossed by Crowell Avenue, Edgewood Avenue and Lincoln Place, mostly unbuilt. E. L. Crowell's cider mill stands on the block between Valley and Kensington Terrace, and the fire department's hose company house stands on the right-hand block on South Prospect. The lowest row of lots, facing Oakland Road, holds a line of small frame houses at the left. Jefferson Avenue enters Valley at the left edge, and Elmwood Avenue and Delaware Avenue enter South Prospect at the lower right. The neighbouring sheets are 39 above, 46 and 47 on the left, 53 below and 55 and 60 on the right.
notes: South Prospect is today Prospect Street, Valley is Valley Street, Academy is Academy Street, Beach is Beach Street, Crowell Avenue is Crowell Place, Edgewood Avenue is Edgewood Place, and Lincoln Place, Kensington Terrace and North Terrace keep their names (OpenStreetMap).
Several junctions along Valley carry residuals of 3 to 4 m, and Oakland Road / Valley Street was left out as 8 m off.
100 ft. Village / township line at the top, Parker Av, Crowell, Edgewood, Lincoln grid, Oakland Rd at the bottom.

sheet-55.description: Sheet 55 shows three long residential blocks of South Orange Township and South Orange Village, in the district that is now the northern part of Maplewood. It is drawn at 50 ft to an inch, twice the detail of the neighbouring sheets, with the street grid turned about a quarter turn so that Prospect runs down the left side and Summit and Richmond avenues run down the middle and right. Vassar Place bounds the sheet at the top and Parker Avenue, drawn with a rounded corner at Prospect, bounds it at the bottom. East of Richmond Avenue the top street is lettered Baldwin Road. The blocks are cut into deep, narrow lots, many of them vacant in 1912. Frame dwellings stand mainly along Summit Avenue and Richmond Avenue and at the corner of Prospect and Parker, with a few auto houses and sheds, and a stone-built dwelling tinted blue near the foot of the left block. A larger group of dwellings, barns and wagon sheds stands at the bottom of the block between Summit and Richmond avenues. A dash-dot line crossing the left block diagonally is lettered as the boundary between South Orange Village and South Orange Township. Water mains (4 in. and 6 in.) are marked beside Prospect Place and Sherman Place at the upper left, where the sheet title occupies a box. The neighbouring sheets named on the margins are 39 and 54 to the left, 41 above, 56 to the right and 60 below.
notes: Drawn at 50 ft to an inch (scale bar 0 to 150 ft); the fitted scale is about 8.0 px/ft, twice that of the 100 ft sheets around it.
Prospect is today Prospect Street (OpenStreetMap).
Vassar Place, and Baldwin Road east of Richmond Avenue, are the street OpenStreetMap calls Baldwin Road; the control points use Baldwin Road at Prospect Street, Summit Avenue and Richmond Avenue.
Sherman Place was not used as control: its junction with Prospect Street lies roughly 15 to 20 m from the drawn one.
The Village and Township boundary line was not checked against the modern municipal line.
50 ft to an inch. Prospect, Summit, Richmond, Vassar Pl (= Baldwin Road), Parker Av; Sherman Pl left out.

sheet-56.description: Sheet 56 shows the end of Parker Avenue and Baldwin Road in South Orange Township, drawn at 50 ft to an inch (scale of feet 0 to 150), with the page turned so that Richmond Avenue runs along the top. Richmond Avenue is drawn only along its south side, with the remainder on sheet 55. Below it a long block numbered 2, the one built-up part of the sheet, is cut into deep, narrow lots with a few frame dwellings and outbuildings, most of them along the Richmond Avenue frontage. Baldwin Road, a 60 ft street, bends across the middle of the page and joins Parker Avenue at the left; Parker Avenue then runs down the left of the sheet, a street of about 50 ft, crossed by Lancaster, Norfolk and Suffolk avenues. West of Parker Avenue the blocks belong to sheet 60 and are drawn without detail. A large unbuilt tract lettered R. H. Ball Est. lies in the middle and lower right, with a single dwelling and coop at its edge on Parker Avenue. Neighbouring sheets are 55 at the top, 60 at the left, 41 at the right and 43 at the bottom.
notes: The modern Baldwin Road is straighter than the drawn road and lies about 5 to 7 m from it in the middle of the sheet.
The top right corner carries the sheet heading 'Vassar Pl.' with South Orange N.J.; it is not a street drawn on this sheet.
The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch; the atlas default is 100 ft.
Control is five junctions, four of them along Parker Avenue and one (Baldwin Road / Richmond Avenue) off that line, so the fit is weakly conditioned (leave-one-out 69 m); treat as low confidence.
50 ft to an inch. Parker Av, Baldwin Rd, Richmond Av; five points, four along Parker Av (weak).

sheet-57.description: Sheet 57 covers part of the Hilton district of South Orange Township (today the southern part of Maplewood), drawn at 100 ft to an inch with the street grid turned so that Springfield Avenue runs down the right edge of the page. The main area is a regular grid of long, narrow residential blocks between Indiana at the top and Wellesley at the bottom, crossed by South Prospect, Princeton and Rutgers, and divided by Revere, Lexington, Franklin and Hilton avenues, with Springfield Avenue along the right. Nearly every block is cut into deep, narrow building lots, most of them still vacant in 1912; frame dwellings are scattered along the cross streets, mostly near Hilton Avenue and Springfield Avenue. The Hilton Hose No. 2 fire house stands on Hilton Avenue between South Prospect and Princeton. The left part of the sheet is an irregular area where Laurel Avenue, Burnett Avenue, Creston Avenue, Concord Avenue and Florida meet the grid at an angle; it holds a few houses, larger lots and open ground towards Burnett Avenue. A dash-dot boundary line crosses this area diagonally from the top edge to the lower left. Across Springfield Avenue, the right margin shows only the ends of Park Avenue, South Prospect Street, Yale Street, Oberlin Street and Rutgers Street, which are drawn in full on sheet 58. Neighbouring sheets are 51 at the top, 65 at the bottom and 58 to the right.
notes: Indiana is today Indiana Street, South Prospect is Prospect Street, Princeton, Rutgers and Wellesley are Princeton, Rutgers and Wellesley Streets, Florida is Florida Street (OpenStreetMap).
Burnett Avenue / Rutgers Street was detected about 7 m from the fit and left out: Burnett Avenue has probably moved there.
A partly cut label at the top edge reads '... Howell Av.'.

Hilton: grid of Indiana (Indiana Street), S. Prospect (Prospect Street), Princeton, Rutgers, Wellesley with Revere, Lexington, Franklin, Hilton and Springfield avenues; Laurel, Burnett, Creston, Concord, Florida at the left. 100 ft. Pilot sheet (ink 80: 31 points, LOO 1.0 m). Burnett / Rutgers rejected (7 m).

sheet-58.description: Sheet 58 covers part of the Hilton district of South Orange Township, today the southern part of Maplewood, drawn at 100 ft to an inch. The street grid is turned so that South Prospect runs along the top of the sheet and Tuscan Road curves down the right edge. In the main part of the sheet, four rows of blocks, numbered 1 to 12, lie between South Prospect, Bowdoin, Yale, Oberlin and Rutgers streets and are crossed by Harvard Avenue and Wellesley Avenue. Nearly every block is divided into narrow building lots, most of them vacant; only a few frame dwellings stand in blocks 1, 2, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10 and 11, with a cluster of buildings on the right edge of block 10 near Tuscan Road. Block 16, a tapering wedge at the lower right between Tuscan Road and the next street, is also divided into lots. At the left, the diagonal avenues Springfield and Cornell and the diagonal South Prospect carry long blocks of narrow lots (blocks 7, 13, 14 and 15) with no buildings. Princeton Street, Rutgers Street and Wellesley Street end at Springfield Avenue at the lower left, where the sheet repeats the margin of sheet 57. Sommer Avenue is cut off at the top left. Neighbouring sheets are 52 above and at the left, 57 below left, 65 below and 59 to the right.
notes: South Prospect is today Prospect Street; Harvard Avenue, Bowdoin, Yale, Oberlin and Rutgers are today Harvard Avenue, Bowdoin Street, Yale Street, Oberlin Street and Rutgers Street (OpenStreetMap).
Wellesley Avenue (the vertical street between Harvard Avenue and Tuscan Road) and Cornell Avenue are not in OpenStreetMap; they were not used as control.
The diagonal Wellesley Avenue, Rutgers and Wellesley Street at the lower left lie on sheet 57 and 65 ground and were not used as control.
Summit Avenue is lettered at the right edge, where it meets Tuscan Road about 20 m from Yale Street.
100 ft. Hilton east of Springfield Av: Park, South Prospect, Yale, Oberlin, Rutgers, Harvard; blank sheet-57 corner masked out.

sheet-59.description: Sheet 59 shows the area south of South Prospect in South Orange Township, in what is now the Maplewood neighbourhood around Summit, Oakview and Madison avenues. It is drawn at 100 ft to an inch with the grid turned so that South Prospect runs across the top and Summit Avenue crosses the middle of the sheet. Above Summit Avenue lie four blocks, numbered 1 to 4, separated by an unnamed avenue (lettered only Av.), Oakview Avenue, Burnett Terrace and Madison Avenue. Blocks 2, 3 and 4 are cut into narrow lots with a handful of frame dwellings, and block 1 holds the Presbyterian chapel near the top. Tuscan Road curves down the left side of the sheet, with the stubs of Bowdoin, Yale, Oberlin and Rutgers streets running off to the left, where the sheet repeats the edge of sheet 58. South of Summit Avenue a street lettered Courter, with a parallel proposed street beside it, runs down past a few dwellings and farm buildings. The rest of the sheet is a large open tract (block 5) lettered Geo F. Johnson, with a dash-dot dividing line and no buildings. At the bottom left Cornell Avenue ends at a house and barns; at the lower right the edge of sheet 60 shows Highland Avenue and Plymouth Place. Neighbouring sheets are 53 above, 58 to the left, 60 to the right and 61 below.
notes: South Prospect is today Prospect Street (OpenStreetMap).
The street lettered Courter is Courter Avenue today; the upper stretch above Summit Avenue carries only the lettering 'Av.'.
The proposed street beside Courter is not in OpenStreetMap.
Bowdoin, Yale, Oberlin and Rutgers streets and Tuscan Road south of Summit Avenue were not used as control; they are drawn in full on sheet 58.
The large tract is lettered Geo F. Johnson (owner).
100 ft. Summit Av, Tuscan Rd, Bowdoin, Yale, Oberlin; large estate below without control. Part ink 60.

sheet-60.description: Sheet 60 covers a district of South Orange Township that is now central Maplewood, around Summit Avenue, Richmond Avenue and Midland Boulevard, drawn at 100 ft to an inch. The street grid is turned so that South Prospect runs diagonally across the top. In the upper left, short blocks (numbers 8 to 11) lie between Madison, Plymouth, Delaware and Elmwood avenues and are laid out in lots with scattered frame dwellings; the largest group of houses stands in block 8 along South Prospect at the upper right, in front of Summit Avenue. South of Richmond Avenue the map becomes a regular grid of long blocks numbered 1 to 7, between Elmwood Avenue and Parker Avenue and cut by Midland Boulevard, Lancaster, Norfolk, Suffolk and Highland avenues. These blocks are subdivided into very narrow lots, almost all vacant in 1912, with only two houses shown. Midland Boulevard runs down the middle and ends in a circle at Highland Avenue at the bottom of the sheet. Baldwin Road enters at the right edge. The left centre is an empty tract lettered Geo. F. Johnson, which continues on sheet 59, and the lower left has Highland Avenue, Plymouth Place and a row of lots. Neighbouring sheets are 53 and 54 above, 55 and 56 to the right, 59 to the left and 62 below.
notes: South Prospect is today Prospect Street (OpenStreetMap).
Delaware Avenue lies on the line of today's Oakland Road; the control points use Oakland Road.
Elmwood Avenue below Richmond Avenue and Midland Boulevard keep their modern names.
The large tract at the left is lettered Geo. F. Johnson (owner).
100 ft. Prospect, Summit, Richmond, Delaware Av (= Oakland Road) grid; blank estate masked out. Part ink 60.

sheet-61.description: Sheet 61 covers the Hilton end of Springfield Avenue in South Orange Township, drawn at 100 ft to an inch with the page turned so that Springfield Avenue, a 70 ft road, runs from the upper left down to a junction with Boyden Avenue at the lower left of centre. Along the western side of Springfield Avenue, in a wedge between it and Academy and Boyden avenues, are the only dense buildings: a post office, the Hilton Park Hotel and frame dwellings, and the Hilton Avenue Church and a school house on lots fronting Boyden Avenue. Tuscan Road and Burnett Avenue come in at the upper left, where the sheet adjoins sheet 65. East of Springfield Avenue lie large unbuilt tracts and farms: Geo. F. Johnson, H. Menzel, Baughfell Kennels, and, at the lower right, the Richard S. Howkins and Anna E. Chase property with a dairy farm and a group of barns. Boyden Avenue continues from the Springfield Avenue junction towards the lower right edge. At the upper right a block of long, narrow lots is laid out along Plymouth Place, between Highland Avenue and Essex Road, still without buildings. Neighbouring sheets are 59 at the top, 60 at the upper right, 62 at the right, 63 at the bottom, 64 at the lower left and 65 at the left.
notes: The street lettered Academy is today part of Tuscan Road (OpenStreetMap); its junction with Boyden Avenue fits the fit to under 1 m.
Springfield Avenue / Tuscan Road appears twice in OpenStreetMap near the upper left junction (about 45 m apart); neither was used.
Control is five junctions, two at the two ends of the sheet.
100 ft. Springfield Av at Hilton, Boyden / Academy (= Tuscan Road), Highland, Plymouth, Essex Rd; mostly open tracts.

sheet-62.description: Sheet 62 covers open farmland and the first laid-out blocks of the Plymouth Place district in South Orange Township, drawn at 100 ft to an inch with the page turned so that Elmwood Avenue runs down the left of centre and Highland Avenue crosses the upper part from left to right. At the upper left, between Plymouth Place, Highland Avenue, Elmwood Avenue and Essex Road, a block numbered 4 is divided into narrow lots with no buildings; a second row of lots lies south of Essex Road and along Highland Avenue east of Elmwood Avenue, where Highland Avenue is crossed by an unnamed street. The rest of the sheet is block 5, large unbuilt tracts running down the page in long strips lettered Thos. Fleming Jr., W. L. Glorieux, Warren P. Ball and John G. Ball. The only buildings are a dwelling on the Fleming tract and farm buildings on the Warren P. Ball and John G. Ball tracts. Boyden Avenue curves across the foot of the sheet from Elmwood Avenue at the lower left to a triangular island at the lower right, where it meets Parker Avenue, which runs down the right edge. Neighbouring sheets are 60 at the top, 61 at the left, 63 at the lower left, 44 at the bottom and 43 at the right.
notes: The unnamed street crossing Highland Avenue east of Elmwood Avenue is probably today's Midland Boulevard (OpenStreetMap), which has no junction with Highland Avenue there in the data and was not used.
Boyden Avenue at the foot of the sheet looked displaced from its modern line on an approximate overlay (about 15 m) and was left out of the control; not measured further.
Control is five junctions, all in the upper half of the sheet; the lower half has none.
100 ft. Highland / Elmwood / Plymouth block and farm tracts; control in the upper half only; Boyden Av and Midland Blvd left out.

sheet-63.description: Sheet 63 covers the Hilton end of Springfield Avenue where South Orange Township meets the town of Irvington, drawn at 100 ft to an inch with the page turned slightly so that Boyden Avenue runs from the top edge down the left side to the lower left corner and Springfield Avenue crosses the foot of the sheet from the lower left to the right. The sheet is mostly farmland and unbuilt tracts: W. L. Glorieux at the upper left, Jane D. Osborne in the upper middle and Richard S. Howkins and Anna E. Chase in the middle, with a few farm buildings. Elmwood Avenue crosses the upper middle from Boyden Avenue to the town boundary, a dash-dot line running up the right of the sheet, east of which lie Franklin, Laurel and Tiffany Place with narrow lots and scattered dwellings. Along the boundary a strip of narrow lots fronts North 43rd Street. The largest building is the Public Service Railway Company's repair shop and car barn on Springfield Avenue, a pink-coloured works with car storage and a machine shop, with a fire-proof pump house and a 50,000 gallon trestle tank beside it. Below Springfield Avenue lie Halstead Avenue and the ends of 44th and 45th streets, with a small cluster of dwellings along 43rd Street. Neighbouring sheets are 44 at the top, 62 at the left, 61 at the lower left, 64 at the bottom.
notes: Printed 'N. 43rd St.' is the part of 43rd Street north of Springfield Avenue; the modern street is 43rd Street (OpenStreetMap).
The boundary lettering along the dash-dot line includes further words that could not be read with confidence; only Newark and Town of Irvington were taken.
Laurel, Tiffany Place and Franklin lie in the Town of Irvington and are not in the reference data (outside South Orange, Maplewood and Millburn); they were not used.

Control is three hand-picked junctions (Boyden / Springfield carried from sheet 61, Boyden / Elmwood and Springfield / 43rd Street); the detector placed junctions in the open ground inside the blocks, so detection was switched off for them. Treat as low confidence.

The detector's positions for Boyden / Elmwood and Boyden / Springfield fell off the drawn junctions by about 18 and 25 m (checked on crops), so the modern line there may be displaced from the drawn one.
100 ft. Springfield Avenue car barn and the Irvington line. Detector misplaced junctions here; three hand-picked or carried points (Boyden / Springfield carried from sheet 61); low confidence.

sheet-64.description: Sheet 64 shows Olympic Park, an amusement park on the line between South Orange Township and the Town of Irvington, at the eastern edge of the Hilton district (now the Maplewood and Irvington border). It is drawn at 100 ft to an inch. A dash-dot line crossing the sheet is the municipal boundary. The park holds a theatre and auditorium, a grand stand, a toboggan slide, a merry-go-round building, a dining and dance hall with cafe and a quarter-mile race track in the form of a long oval. Rows of small buildings line the top edge along Halstead Avenue and the foot of 43rd, 44th and 45th streets, with larger works buildings at the upper right. Springfield Avenue runs diagonally across the upper left, with a fire station (Hilton Hose No. 1) beside Boyden Avenue at the left edge. The rest of the sheet is large estates, lettered Susan Mc Donough, Wm Becker, John A. Becker Est. and F. A. Haussmann, bounded at the bottom by Boyden Avenue. 40th Street runs down the right edge, with Leslie Place and Olympic Terrace branching from it, and a brook is drawn along the lower right edge. Neighbouring sheets are 61 and 65 at the left, 63 above and 66 below.
notes: Drawn at 100 ft to an inch; only three junctions were found (40th Street with Leslie Place and Olympic Terrace, and Boyden Avenue with Springfield Avenue), so the placement is weak.
Halstead, 43rd, 44th and 45th streets have no junction with a listed modern street in OpenStreetMap and were not used as control.
The large lettering near the park reads 'Newark ... Vol ... Town of Irvington' along the boundary line; the part after 'Newark' could not be read with confidence.
100 ft. Olympic Park (amusement park and race track) between Springfield Av, Boyden Av and 40th St.

sheet-65.description: Sheet 65 covers the Hilton district of South Orange Township, now the Maplewood and Irvington border, drawn at 100 ft to an inch on a smaller scan than the neighbouring sheets, with the grid turned so that Wellesley runs along the top. In the upper centre a regular grid of blocks numbered 3 to 5 and 8 to 9 lies between Lexington, Franklin and Hilton avenues and is crossed by Tuscan and Vermont streets; the blocks are cut into narrow lots, mostly vacant, with a few dwellings. Burnett Avenue runs diagonally from the top left to the bottom centre, with deep lots on its west side held by named owners (E R Lakey, J. H. Van Ness, Henry Marion, J. Denninger, B. D. Huggan, A. Fatzler, J. Zellers, H. C. Boeger, Wm. T. Brown, J. F. Dean) and a florist's greenhouses (Louis Becker and Son) at the upper left. Where Burnett Avenue meets Academy and Boyden Avenue at the bottom the sheet shows more houses, and block 11 holds the Christian Church. Springfield runs down the right side with Tuscan Road joining it from the upper right, and blocks 6 and 7 at the right lie between Wellesley Avenue, Tuscan Place and Cornell Avenue. The large area at the left is the J. Grant Est. Neighbouring sheets are 57 above, 58 at the upper right, 61 at the right, 64 below and 66 at the left.
notes: Wellesley, Tuscan and Vermont are today Wellesley Street, Tuscan Street and Vermont Street (OpenStreetMap).
Academy is today Tuscan Road in OpenStreetMap, and the street lettered Tuscan Road at the right is also Tuscan Road.
Burnett Avenue / Franklin Avenue was detected about 10 m from the fit and left out.
The scan is smaller than the other sheets of the atlas (7350 by 8751 px); the fitted scale is about 3.45 px/ft.
Owners' names on the long lots are listed in the description, not as place names.
100 ft, smaller scan (7350 x 8751, 3.45 px/ft). Wellesley, Tuscan (Academy), Vermont, Burnett, Boyden.

sheet-66.description: Sheet 66 shows the southernmost corner of South Orange Township (today Maplewood) on the Essex County and Union County line, drawn at 100 ft to an inch. Boyden Avenue runs up the right edge and meets Stuyvesant Avenue at the lower right, where 40th Street leaves to the right and Stuyvesant Avenue turns down off the sheet; a fire alarm box and hydrant mark the junction. Stuyvesant Avenue runs along the bottom edge, with a stream drawn in blue just above it. The narrow strip between the stream and Stuyvesant Avenue is lettered Newark Vol. Five, Town of Irvington, and carries a row of small buildings. A dash-dot line marked Essex County and Union County crosses the lower left of the sheet diagonally to Stuyvesant Avenue. The rest of the sheet is open land divided into a few large tracts with their owners' names: the Hugo Menzel estate in the upper middle with a pond, a dwelling, stables, a greenhouse and outbuildings; the Henry Voss holdings along Boyden Avenue with dwellings, sheds and hen houses; the large Eugene & John H. Van Ness tract with a storage building; and the R. S. Howell and A. T. Ball lots along the stream, each with a dwelling and sheds. Small dwellings and outbuildings also stand along Boyden Avenue. Sheet 65 adjoins at the top and sheet 64 on the right.
notes: Modern streets laid out over these tracts carry the 1912 owners' names: Menzel Avenue, Van Ness Terrace and Van Ness Court.

Placed from two points only: the 40th Street / Boyden Avenue / Stuyvesant Avenue junction (hand-picked) and the county line on Stuyvesant Avenue taken from the boundary between Irvington and Union Township parcels (helmert, fitted scale 2 percent below the atlas value); low confidence.

Southern corner on the Essex / Union county line: Boyden Av, Stuyvesant Av, 40th St; Menzel, Voss, Van Ness tracts. 100 ft. Two points: hand-picked junction and the county line on Stuyvesant Av from parcels (helmert); low confidence.
